deviations: AMCEs estimated by OLS of the forced-choice indicator on dummies for all seven attributes (main effects only), SEs clustered by respondent (fixest), rather than with the cjoint package (not installed). The German design restricts Language=None from co-occurring with an internal origin (enforced in the German data, not in the U.S. data); no language x origin interaction was added, which affects only the language/origin coefficients in principle, not the reason-for-migration AMCEs in expectation.

Sample: Qualtrics survey-preview responses dropped; every profile with a non-missing forced choice is kept (partial completers included); duplicated psid values (1 US, 6 DE) were not removed. respondents_* = distinct respondents with at least one answered choice; choice_tasks_* = profile rows entering the estimation.
notes: Attempt-1 was an exploratory run (data structure: Qualtrics conjoint export, F-k-j attribute names / F-k-p-j levels for 9 tasks x 2 profiles; task-1 choice in force_choice, tasks 2-9 in Q184..Q198). Final script reshapes both conjoint files to profile level, maps German labels to English, baseline Economic opportunity for reason, and estimates full-model AMCEs. Outcome is the binary forced choice (not the 1-7 rating). Only the conjoint CSVs were used; study-2 and follow-up files and the .dat design files were inspected for structure only (design files read on host to learn levels/restrictions).
